THE ROW HEIGHT IS SET BY THE IMAGE'S OWN ASPECT, NOT BY THE TEXT. This is the correction to the first attempt, which shipped a 1475x2048 portrait master and made the first block visibly taller than the other five. `media-with-text` is a CSS grid with one row per block; `.media-with-text__media` carries no aspect-ratio of its own, so the img's intrinsic aspect drives its height and the row grows to whichever column is taller. Every other image in this section is a square master, so every other row is image-driven and square at desktop widths. A 0.72 master is 1.389x its own width tall and towered over all of them.

MEASURED, by overriding the img's aspect-ratio in the live DOM and reading `grid-template-rows` back at six widths. Intro row height, in px:

  viewport   text alone   with 1:1   with 1475:2048 (shipped first, wrong)
  390        493          843        979
  768        448          1152       1425
  1024       512          512        628
  1280       528          580        805
  1440       514          660        917
  1920       514          708        983

Siblings at 1440 are 802 / 660 / 753 / 729 / 753 and at 1920 are 778 / 708 / 753 / 708 / 708. At 1:1 the intro row lands on 660 and 708 — identical to the square siblings and no longer the tallest anywhere. The intro copy is short (514px at 1440), so this block is fully image-driven at every width from 1280 up.

THE EARLIER '0.559 AT 1024' READING WAS WRONG. The first pass measured the intro box at 452x808 on a page that had only just finished loading, and a portrait master was cut to clear a slice that was never there: with a square master the 1024 box is 452x512 (0.883), a 5.9% side crop each edge, not 22%. The lesson from a-number-checked-only-against-itself-gets-believed applies to layout numbers too — the DOM override above is a second, independent signal and it disagreed with the first.

SQUARE CROP CHOSEN. Four squares were rendered and compared with the 0.883 crop box drawn on: the untouched 2048 frame carries too much out-of-focus hair on the left; y500 cuts the eye at the top edge. x573-2048 y280-1755 keeps the left/right framing Malcolm already approved and loses only the top of the head and a little neck — eye, nose, mouth, chin and the fingers all sit inside the 0.883 box.
